title: The story behind the new container shipping rates
description: A look at why container rates jumped 40% in two weeks, who pays for it, and what it means for consumer goods this fall.
transcript: Today's story is about shipping rates, which have done something quite unusual over the past two weeks. They've jumped roughly forty percent. Now, this is the kind of statistic that, if you read it without context, sounds either impossible or boring — and as I'll explain, it's neither...

title: Why the courts care about subway turnstile data
description: An obscure ruling on transit data is reshaping privacy law for cities everywhere.
transcript: Subway turnstile data. Three words you've probably never thought about together. But starting tomorrow, an unusual federal court ruling has the potential to change how every U.S. city collects, stores, and shares public-transit data...

title: The 100-year flood that comes every six years
description: A meteorologist explains what changed about FEMA's flood maps.
transcript: Flood maps. Boring topic. Crucial topic. The phrase '100-year flood' is something you've heard, and you probably misunderstand it...

title: When clock skew broke our payment processor
description: A subtle bug where database replicas drifted 12 seconds apart silently corrupted hundreds of payment records.
transcript: Welcome back to Edge Cases. This week's bug is about a clock — specifically, twelve seconds. Twelve seconds of clock skew between a primary and a replica database. That sounds harmless. It was not harmless...

title: The TLS bug that took down half of Reddit
description: A lesson on certificate-chain validation gone wrong.
transcript: TLS. Three letters. Fundamental. Boring until it isn't. This week, we're going to talk about a TLS bug that, for about ninety minutes, took down half of Reddit...

title: Lin Chen of Sundial Labs on year five
description: After her seed round in 2020, Lin built quietly. Today: $40M ARR, profitable, and 28 employees. The story is unusual.
transcript: My guest today is Lin Chen, founder of Sundial Labs. Lin and I have known each other for eight years. The reason I wanted her on the show is that her trajectory is uncommon — quiet, profitable, and slow...

title: The librarian who saved a town's records
description: A small-town librarian spent 23 years restoring water-damaged county records. She finished last week.
transcript: Margaret Hayes is sixty-eight years old. For twenty-three of those years, she has been the head — and at times only — librarian at the Morgan County Library in eastern Kentucky...

title: Edwin Brady on Idris and dependent types in production
description: Idris creator on the practical state of dependent typing, ten years on.
transcript: Edwin Brady is the creator of Idris and Idris 2. He's been working on dependent types since the early 2000s, and this conversation centers on what's actually deployable today...
